title: Prawn Linguine
subtitle: Garlic, chilli, and prawn linguine in 20 minutes
excerpt: Raw king prawns sautéed with garlic, chilli, white wine, and cherry tomatoes, tossed through linguine with a handful of parsley. One of the fastest restaurant-quality pasta dishes to make at home.

recipe.sourceNotes: Prawn pasta dishes appear all around the Mediterranean coast. The combination of garlic, white wine, chilli, and shellfish over pasta is particularly associated with Southern Italian coastal cooking. The technique is simple: the prawns take only 2 to 3 minutes to cook and the rest is just a quick pan sauce. The pasta water is the secret emulsifier: a splash starchens the sauce and helps it cling.

content.text: Cook the pasta until one minute short of the packet time: it finishes cooking in the pan sauce. Reserve a mugful of starchy pasta water before draining. Prawns are done the moment they are pink all the way through. Pull them off the heat immediately: overcooked prawns turn rubbery within seconds.
Cook the linguine in a large pan of heavily salted boiling water for 1 minute less than the packet time. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute until the garlic is just beginning to colour.
Add the cherry tomatoes and white wine. Simmer for 2 minutes. Add the prawns in a single layer. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink all the way through, turning once.
Add the drained linguine and a splash of pasta water. Toss over the heat for 1 minute until the sauce coats the pasta. Add the lemon juice and parsley. Season with salt and serve immediately.
